clue.text: Moody chap is more disposed to get tense

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A sulky man is ever more inclined to become uptight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moody' looks like a description of the chap, but it is the definition; 'disposed' rearranges CHAPISMORE with T added.
explanation.definitionFit: A moody film or piece of music is one full of atmosphere, evoking a strong feeling.

clue.text: One on spree ultimately not flipping solvent!

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word not is read backwards
ultimately points to the final letter of spree

explanation.surface: Someone out on a binge ends up not getting angry, merely dissolving things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link placing one piece after another; the exclamation mark points at the playful sense of 'solvent' as a chemical rather than financially sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a common chemical solvent, used for example in nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Dull thing that doesn't end

indicators.note: a thing that doesn't end loses its last letter, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: matter means stuff or a thing

explanation.surface: A boring object that drags on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte finish is a dull, non-glossy one, as on photographs or paint.

clue.text: Look adopted by gentleman with trendy cut

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the look goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman
in means fashionable, trendy
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A gentleman takes on a new look with a fashionable haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a haircut, but it is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime cut of beef taken from the loin.

clue.text: Suspicions created by hotel meals lacking a starter

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: lacking a starter means without the first letter, a nod to a meal without its first course

parts.note: lunches are meals

explanation.surface: Guests suspect something when the hotel serves meals with no first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunches are intuitive feelings or suspicions without firm proof.

clue.text: Lacking energy, otter tries swimming to get a drink

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken from the pool
swimming means moving about freely, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired otter attempts a swim before having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E out of OTTERTRIES and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ristretto is a very short, strong shot of espresso coffee.

clue.text: Chef's prime chop that is rubbery on top and harder to bite into

parts.note: the prime, or first, letter of Chef's
to hew is to chop
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: on top points to the first letter of rubbery, the one at the top in a down clue

explanation.surface: A chef's best cut of meat is rubbery and tougher to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chewier needs more chewing, so it is tougher to sink the teeth into.

clue.text: Card-sharp initially changing hand with someone at the table?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of changing and hand

parts.note: an eater is someone sitting at a dining table

explanation.surface: A card player swaps his hand to fool someone across the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the table' suggests a card table, but it is the dining table where an eater sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-sharp is a swindler at cards, someone who cheats other players.

clue.text: Covert network in clubs certain to get snubbed

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: snubbed suggests cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: destined means certain to happen

explanation.surface: A secret circle within the clubs is sure to be cold-shouldered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just sets the network beside clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine means kept secret or done stealthily, the same as covert.

clue.text: Supply teas now, and a piece of cake!

indicators.note: read as supple-y, meaning flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Serve tea now, along with a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb to provide, but it is the adverb from supple, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal idiom for an easy task, as is a piece of cake.

clue.text: American involved in three fantastic fights, give or take

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the letter goes within the other pieces
fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: bouts are boxing fights

explanation.surface: A US boxer takes part in three amazing contests, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give or take' sounds like a stray aside, but it is the definition, meaning approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereabouts means approximately, near enough, as does give or take.

clue.text: Person residing in a European house

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so the person goes within the other letters

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person

explanation.surface: Someone living in a European home.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling place, a home.

clue.text: Unmarried parent, experienced in a different way

indicators.note: unmarried means without M, the abbreviation for married

parts.note: a mother is a parent
wise means made knowledgeable by experience

explanation.surface: A single mother has learned a lot from life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmarried' looks like it describes the parent, but it removes M (married).
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means differently, or by other means.

clue.text: Think obsessively about diet, primarily, and about keeping fit

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of diet

parts.note: keeping well means staying healthy, fit
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone frets about dieting and staying in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on something is to keep brooding over it in one's mind.

clue.text: Poets, as a rule, worked without them regularly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go around the others
worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are rearranged
regularly means every other letter of them is taken

explanation.surface: As a rule, poets have done without them on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the others rather than lacking them.
explanation.definitionFit: Laureates are poets laureate, those officially honoured as poets of a nation.

clue.text: Release a collection of songs at no cost

parts.note: a set is the group of songs played in a performance
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A band gives away an album without charging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like the music sense, issuing a record; it means liberate.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to release from captivity.

clue.text: Boy grabs 24 hours in Paris for a visit

indicators.note: grabs means seizes and holds, so the boy goes around the other piece

parts.note: a son is a boy
jour is French for day

explanation.surface: A lad snatches a day in Paris for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere, a visit.

clue.text: One who cleans rubbish up after New Year's Day

indicators.note: after puts the rubbish behind the day in the answer

parts.note: 1 January written as JAN I

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A cleaner tidies up the litter after the New Year party.
explanation.walkthrough: Write January 1 as JAN plus Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a caretaker whose job includes cleaning a building.

clue.text: Geordie that was close with southern relatives?

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE
phew is the exclamation of relief after a narrow escape

explanation.surface: A Newcastle man, after a near miss, joins his family from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that was close' is not a description but the exclamation itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephews are a person's brothers' or sisters' sons, so family members.

clue.text: Wild young politician accepts short prompt

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the politician goes around the other piece

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: on cue means promptly, at just the right time

explanation.surface: A youthful politician welcomes a brief cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young politician' reads as one phrase, but 'young' belongs with 'Wild' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion cub is the offspring of a wild big cat.

clue.text: Rock singer's age-old stories, all notedly spicy in the middle

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is, so the clue reads Rock singer is age-old stories plus letters; fair because the definition itself is just the singer of the rock

parts.note: lore is traditional tales and knowledge

indicators.note: in the middle points to the centre letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A rock star's old tales are all famously racy at their core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock singer' suggests a pop star, but it is the siren of a Rhine rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a legendary siren who sang from a rock on the Rhine, luring boatmen to ruin.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in source of sugar and pepper

indicators.note: invested in means put into, so the money goes inside the other piece

parts.note: sugar cane is a source of sugar
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: Overseas cash is put into sugar and spice businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper ground into a spice.

clue.text: Bulk of important record held by private landlord

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so these pieces go inside private

parts.note: inner means private, personal

indicators.note: bulk of means most of, so the last letter goes

parts.note: key means important
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Most of a vital document is kept by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like a soldier, but means inner.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs a pub or inn, the British sense of landlord.

clue.text: Dog endlessly pursuing evasive rodent

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the dog comes after

parts.note: coy means evasive, reluctant to give details

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A dog keeps chasing a slippery rat.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American aquatic rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Insect about to cover over 1,000 miles

indicators.note: to cover means to go around, so about surrounds the other letters

parts.note: ca is circa, about
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
M is the Roman numeral for 1,000

explanation.surface: A bug is about to fly more than a thousand miles.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a butterfly named for the white comma-shaped mark on its wing.

clue.text: Nurse has right permit

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
a title is a legal right, as to property

explanation.surface: A nurse has the right to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them the right or allow them to do something.

clue.text: Complaints in muscles overwhelming some guys

indicators.note: overwhelming means covering over, so the muscles go around the other piece

parts.note: lats are the latissimus dorsi back muscles
men are some guys

explanation.surface: Grumbles about muscle strain swamp a group of lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Laments are expressions of grief or complaint.

clue.text: Revive and reshape it with secateurs

indicators.note: reshape means form anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bring a plant back to life by pruning it with garden shears.
explanation.definitionFit: To resuscitate is to bring someone back to consciousness or life.
